candidate.title: SSB-Seq
candidate.scope: The single Illumina SSB-Seq schematic: genomic DNA nick labeling with digoxigenin, DNA isolation/random shearing, anti-digoxigenin capture and recovered DNA. The initial highlighted-break icon is descriptive. The paper clarifies the downstream sequencing interface and substrate limitations; its separate DSB-Seq workflow and ETO application are outside the depicted route.

states.label: Genomic DNA containing single-strand breaks
features: Already isolated genomic DNA is drawn as a blue duplex with a discontinuity in one strand. The leftmost highlighted-break icon explains the biological target; it is not an independently processed input.
The next reaction labels breaks with a free 3′-OH suitable for nick translation; it does not cover all damaged DNA termini.

§2.1 Overview of Single-Strand Break (SSB)-Seq, b00010; Figure 1a caption, b00011
evidence.quote: Samples were subjected to nick-translation by DNA polymerase I in the presence of deoxynucleotide triphosphates including digoxigenin labeled dUTP. To restrict labeling to a small patch of DNA in order to increase the resolution of mapping, dideoxynucleotides were included in the reaction to inhibit excessive chain elongation by DNA polymerase I. DNA was sheared by sonication and labeled fragments were immunoprecipitated with anti-digoxigenin antibody, purified and subjected to Illumina library preparation and sequencing (Figure 1a).

operations.label: DNA Pol I, dU-digoxigenin, and dNTPs
operations.description: Nick translation incorporates digoxigenin-labeled dUTP into genomic DNA at labelable single-strand breaks, converting nicked DNA into locally tagged DNA. DNA polymerase I is the catalyst; nucleotides are labeling reagents.
operations.mechanism: DNA polymerase I nick translation requires a free 3′-OH. The paper specifies dideoxynucleotides to inhibit excessive elongation and restrict labeling to a small patch.
operations.information_effect: Covalently incorporated digoxigenin marks a DNA region near a pre-existing labelable break for later enrichment. Coverage depends on having a suitable 3′-OH; unprocessed Top1 cleavage termini and other blocked 3′ termini are not labeled by this interface.

operations.label: DNA isolation and random shearing
operations.description: The already labeled DNA is purified and randomly fragmented, yielding short labeled and unlabeled genomic fragments. The paper identifies sonication as the fragmentation process. The drawn post-label “DNA isolation” is interpreted as purification of the labeled DNA; initial genomic DNA isolation precedes the input state.
operations.information_effect: Labeled patches remain carried by genomic fragments; the newly generated fragment ends are not themselves the original SSB coordinates.

operations.label: Immunoprecipitate with anti-digoxigenin antibody
operations.description: Anti-digoxigenin antibody binds the digoxigenin on labeled DNA and supports selective recovery of those fragments from the sheared mixture. Pale fragments around the antibody depict background rather than an alternative target workflow.
operations.mechanism: Antibody recognition of incorporated digoxigenin; Protein G-Sepharose recovers the immunocomplexes in the primary implementation.
operations.information_effect: Enriches genomic fragments carrying digoxigenin incorporated at labelable breaks. Biological coverage remains constrained by the nick-translation substrate requirement.

operations.label: DNA (recovery after immunoprecipitation)
operations.description: Recover and purify DNA from the captured immunocomplexes to produce the free DNA shown at the right. Recovery chemistry is supplied by the primary paper; the drawing labels only the DNA product.
operations.information_effect: Recovered genomic DNA supplies the sequence for a downstream Illumina library. Mapping its reads identifies regions associated with labeled breaks. Random shearing and a labeled patch, rather than direct sequencing of a marked original break end, limit positional interpretation; the catalogue states that break locations cannot be determined accurately.
